drills.q: State the three perceptual latency thresholds for voice agents and the human behavior that sets them.
drills.a: ~200ms is the natural human turn-taking gap; under ~800ms a reply feels responsive/natural; past ~800ms pauses become noticeable; past ~1500ms conversation breaks down â€” users repeat themselves, talk over the agent, or assume the line dropped.

drills.q: List the six stages of a cascaded voice round trip with typical budgets.
drills.a: Uplink+jitter 50-100ms; endpointing 100-500ms; STT partial <250ms; LLM first token 100-600ms; TTS first audio 90-313ms; network hops 50-200ms per vendor leg.

drills.q: What's the difference between VAD and endpointing, in one sentence each?
drills.a: VAD: classifies a single ~20-30ms audio frame as speech or non-speech. Endpointing: decides whether the caller's entire turn has ended and the agent should respond â€” consuming VAD output plus transcript finality plus semantics as inputs.

drills.q: Your agent both interrupts users AND leaves long dead-air pauses. Why won't another silence-threshold pass fix it, and what will?
drills.a: The two complaints pull opposite directions on the same knob, proving silence duration carries no hesitation-vs-completion information. The fix is a semantic layer: score utterance completeness from lexical/syntactic/prosodic content (semantic_vad-style eagerness or a turn-detection model), keeping acoustic VAD for mic gating/noise rejection.

drills.q: Walk through the barge-in loop with its deadline, and name the prerequisite that stops self-interruption.
drills.a: Detect user speech during playback â†’ stop agent audio within ~150ms â†’ flush TTS buffer + queued audio â†’ cancel in-flight LLM generation â†’ reroute new audio to STT. Prerequisite: acoustic echo cancellation, else TTS leaking through the speakerphone mic registers as user speech and the agent barges in on itself.

drills.q: Why is LLM total generation time irrelevant to voice responsiveness, and what metric replaces it?
drills.a: Audio plays while tokens continue streaming, so total generation hides under playback; only time-to-first-token gates responsiveness because chunking and TTS can't start before it. Reduce via fast model tier (100-200 vs 250-600ms), prompt caching, regional colocation, and speaking filler during tool calls.

drills.q: Compare cascaded and speech-to-speech stacks on auditability, model choice, latency, and cost.
drills.a: Cascaded: ground-truth per-stage transcripts (debuggable), any model including fine-tunes, VPC-resident, $0.0095-$0.17/min predictable; ~1400ms sequential â†’ 500-700ms streamed. S2S: ~600-900ms end-to-end, native prosody and interruption, but transcript is a derived artifact, model choice locked to vendor, ~182x per-minute cost spread across providers.

drills.q: p50 response time is 420ms, yet CSAT dropped. Name the measurement mistake and two likely tail sources.
drills.a: Reporting the mean/median instead of p95/p99 â€” subjective experience anchors on worst turns; 400ms averages routinely hide 2.5s tails. Likely tail sources: endpointing policy on hesitant speakers, uncached prompts/cold starts, TTS vendor variance (tight-IQR vendors trade slower medians for fewer outliers), multi-vendor region hops.

drills.q: An enterprise support line wants a voice bot. Recommend an architecture and defend it against 'just use the realtime API.'
drills.a: Default cascaded: compliance needs per-stage transcripts (what was heard vs answered), domain fine-tuned models stay swappable, VPC residency possible, cost predictable ($0.0095-$0.17/min vs ~182x S2S spread). Offer hybrid if feel matters: S2S conversation plus parallel STT for the audit transcript. S2S-only wins when conversational feel is the product and traceability requirements are light.

drills.q: In the energy-VAD exercise: why does pre-roll capture exist, and what production component replaces the RMS energy gate?
drills.a: Pre-roll exists because the trigger always fires after speech onset â€” you learn speech started only once it started, so you retain ~200ms of prior audio to protect word onsets from front-end clipping. Production swaps the RMS threshold for a neural probability (Silero/Cobra) but keeps the identical state-machine skeleton: pre-roll, hangover hysteresis, speech_end emission.

drills.q: A reasoning model needs 8 seconds of thinking before answering. Can it live inside a voice agent?
drills.a: Only with explicit design: spoken filler ('let me check that') plus progress sounds while thinking, or route such queries off the voice path entirely. Silent 8s dead air guarantees the user talks over the thinking, corrupting the turn. It's an architectural constraint on which models go where in the voice path, not a tuning detail.

drills.q: Why does narrowband telephony audio (8 kHz) hurt more than just transcription accuracy?
drills.a: 8kHz/4kHz-Nyquist loses consonant detail, raising WER versus the 16 kHz models expect (Silero supports both rates precisely because of this mismatch); higher WER cascades into repair loops and longer conversations, so codec choice is part of the quality budget. Upsampling doesn't recover lost information, and the bandwidth saving is irrelevant next to model latencies.

drills.q: Explain the architectural bet Cartesia made with Sonic's state-space-model TTS versus a transformer-based competitor, and why it matters for p99.
drills.a: SSMs process sequences more efficiently than transformer attention, giving Sonic consistently low latency including at the tail (p99), not just a good median -- Sonic 3.5 reports 75-90ms time-to-first-audio, which matters because p99 determines the worst-case caller experience, not the average one.
